Resources/ControlsPage_Paragraph1_Text: Controls let you take actions and make choices. The <bold>Next</bold> and <bold>Back</bold> buttons in this guide are a type of control. You'll get to try out several different types of controls on this page.
Resources/ControlsPage_Paragraph2_Text: To move between them, press the <bold>Up</bold> and <bold>Down arrow</bold> keys, or press <bold>Tab</bold> or <bold>Shift + Tab</bold>. Using the <bold>Tab</bold> key will work to move between controls even when you're not using a screen reader like Narrator.
Resources/ControlsPage_Paragraph3_Text: In some cases, the <bold>Up</bold> and <bold>Down arrow</bold> keys may move you through a list of choices in a control. Once you get to the choice you want, press <bold>Enter</bold>. You'll also press <bold>Enter</bold> to use controls that only have two states, like a toggle or check box.
Resources/ControlsPage_SearchBox_Header: This is a search box text label
Resources/ControlsPage_SearchBox_Text: Type the name of a continent

Resources/ControlsPage_ToggleSwitch_Head: This is a toggle text label
Resources/EnteringTextPage_Paragraph1_Te: Text boxes are places on a page where you can enter your own text. You'll find them a lot in forms. When you land inside a text box, scan mode will automatically turn off.
Resources/EnteringTextPage_Paragraph2_Te: After you're done typing, you can use the <bold>Down arrow</bold> key to keep going. If you're in a multi-line text box, you may need to press the <bold>Down arrow</bold> several times to get out of the box. Once you're out of the text box, scan mode will turn back on.
Resources/EnteringTextPage_Paragraph3_Te: There's a single-line text box below. Go ahead and practice entering text.
Resources/EnteringTextPage_TextBox_Heade: This is a label for a text box.
Resources/EnteringTextPage_TextBox_Text: You're now inside the text box, so you can start typing
Resources/ExploreKeyboardPage_Paragraph1: Throughout this guide, you'll hear keyboard shortcuts and Narrator commands that may be useful to you. They'll sound like this.
Resources/ExploreKeyboardPage_Paragraph3: That means press and hold <bold>Caps lock</bold>, then press the number <bold>1</bold> key. This shortcut turns on input learning.
Resources/ExploreKeyboardPage_Paragraph4: Input learning tells you what keys you're pressing on your keyboard, as well as the Narrator command associated with them. To turn it off, press and hold <bold>Caps lock</bold>, then press the number <bold>1</bold> key.
Resources/ExploreKeyboardPage_Paragraph5: You'll learn many commands as you go through this guide. You can view a full list of Narrator commands anytime by pressing <bold>Caps lock + F1</bold>.
Resources/ExploreKeyboardPage_Paragraph6: Press <bold>Enter</bold> on the <bold>Next</bold> button to go to the next screen.
Resources/HeadingsPage_Paragraph1_Text: In addition to using the <bold>Up</bold> and <bold>Down arrow</bold> keys, you can also move to different sections on a page using headings. Here are some examples of how different heading levels are read out.
Resources/HeadingsPage_Paragraph2_Text: This is a heading level 1, which is often used for page titles.
Resources/HeadingsPage_Paragraph3_Text: This is a heading level 2, which is often used for section headings within pages.
Resources/HeadingsPage_Paragraph4_Text: To move to the next heading, press the <bold>H key</bold>. To go back to the previous heading, press <bold>Shift + H</bold>. You may need to do that on this page.
Resources/HeadingsPage_Paragraph5_Text: You can try this now, or go to the next screen.
Resources/LandmarksPage_Paragraph1_Text: Landmarks are like containers that enclose similar parts of a page or app, and you can navigate directly to them. They can be a grouping of similar elements, like buttons or blocks of text, or a single element like a search box. Landmarks are super common on the web.
Resources/LandmarksPage_Paragraph2_Text: There are generally three types of landmarks:
Resources/LandmarksPage_Paragraph3_Text: Navigation landmarks let you move between different parts of an app. The <bold>Next</bold> and <bold>Back</bold> buttons on this page are inside a navigation landmark.
Resources/LandmarksPage_Paragraph4_Text: Main landmarks are an app's content. The words are part of this page's main landmark.
Resources/LandmarksPage_Paragraph5_Text: Search landmarks are typically search boxes. We'll talk more about these later.
Resources/LandmarksPage_Paragraph6_Text: To move to the next landmark, press the <bold>D</bold> key. To go back to the previous landmark, press <bold>Shift + D</bold>. You may need to do that on this page.
Resources/LandmarksPage_Paragraph7_Text: You can try this now, or go to the next screen.
Resources/NarratorCommandsPage_Paragraph: To browse a list of Narrator commands, press <bold>Narrator + F1</bold>.
To open Narrator settings, press <bold>Windows logo key + Ctrl + N</bold>.
Let's go over a few Narrator commands that let you customize what and how Narrator reads things to you. Here they are.
Increase Narrator voice speed by pressing <bold>Narrator + the Plus sign</bold>.
Decrease voice speed by pressing <bold>Narrator + the Minus sign</bold>.
Hear the current item by pressing <bold>Narrator + Tab</bold>.
Hear the title of a window by pressing <bold>Narrator + T</bold>.
To go to the top of a window, press <bold>Narrator + Home</bold>.
To go to the bottom of a window, press <bold>Narrator + End</bold>.
To read from wherever you are, press <bold>Narrator + R</bold>.
To read from the top of the window, press <bold>Narrator + W</bold>.

Resources/NarratorHomePage_BodyTextBlock: This is Narrator Home, where you can get help, access your settings, and learn about new features. Narrator is a screen reader that describes aloud what's on your screen, so you can use that information to navigate your device. To start or stop Narrator, press the <bold>Windows logo key + Ctrl + Enter</bold>. Explore the sections below to get started.
Resources/NarratorHomePage_FeedbackTileB: Help improve Narrator. Press Narrator key + Alt + F to give feedback anytime.
Resources/NarratorHomePage_MinimizeSetti: Minimize Narrator Home to the system tray
Resources/NarratorHomePage_SettingsTileB: Customize Narrator. Press Windows logo key + Ctrl + N to access settings anytime.
Resources/NarratorHomePage_UserGuideTile: View the complete Narrator guide online.
Resources/NarratorHomePage_WhatsNewTileB: Get an overview of new and updated features.
Resources/NarratorKeyPage_Paragraph1_Tex: You may have noticed that <bold>Caps lock</bold> is an essential key in many Narrator commands. When used in Narrator, <bold>Caps lock</bold> is also known as the <bold>Narrator</bold> key. <bold>Insert</bold> can also serve as your <bold>Narrator</bold> key.
Resources/NarratorKeyPage_Paragraph2_Tex: So, when you encounter a command that uses the <bold>Narrator</bold> key, just remember that you can use either <bold>Caps lock</bold> or <bold>Insert</bold>. The <bold>Narrator</bold> key will be referred to as simply "<bold>Narrator</bold>" in commands from now on.
Resources/NavigatingAppsPage_Paragraph1_: The next few skills work whether or not you're using a screen reader like Narrator.
Resources/NavigatingAppsPage_Paragraph3_: When you have several apps open, you can switch between them by pressing <bold>Alt + Tab</bold>. You may need to hold down <bold>Alt</bold>, and press the <bold>Tab</bold> key several times to find the app you want. If you try the shortcuts on this page, use <bold>Alt + Tab</bold> to get back to this guide.
Resources/NavigatingAppsPage_Paragraph5_: Pressing the <bold>Windows logo key</bold> gets you to the Start menu, and to the search box on your taskbar. From there, you can enter the name of the app you want to find. Then, use the <bold>Up</bold> and <bold>Down arrow</bold> keys to move through the options, and press <bold>Enter</bold> to select one.
Resources/NavigatingAppsPage_Paragraph7_: To close an app, press <bold>Alt + F4</bold>. You may need to press the <bold>Fn</bold> key before you do this.
Resources/QuickStartOfflinePage_BadJsonE: Something happened on our end, and the rest of Narrator QuickStart isn't available right now. Access an online version of the <Hyperlink url="http://aka.ms/NarratorGuide">Narrator user guide</Hyperlink> anytime.
Resources/QuickStartOfflinePage_OfflineE: There's an in-depth version of this guide online. Once you're connected to the internet, restart Narrator to view it.
Resources/ReadingWordsPage_Paragraph1_Te: You can review individual characters in words by using the <bold>Left</bold> and <bold>Right arrow</bold> keys. This is a great way to check spelling.
Resources/ReadingWordsPage_Paragraph2_Te: To read word by word, press <bold>Ctrl + Left arrow</bold> or <bold>Ctrl + Right arrow</bold>.
Resources/ReadingWordsPage_Paragraph3_Te: You can try this now, or go to the next screen.
Resources/ScanModePage_Paragraph1_Text: Scan mode is a feature of Narrator that lets you use just a few keys to move around your screen.
Resources/ScanModePage_Paragraph2_Text: Scan mode is already on unless you turned it off. You can practice turning it off and on by pressing <bold>Caps lock + Spacebar</bold>. Brief sounds will play when you use that command to help you quickly know what mode you're in. Be sure it's turned on for the remainder of this guide.
Resources/ScanModePage_Paragraph3_Text: While you're in scan mode, you can press the <bold>Up</bold> and <bold>Down arrow</bold> keys to read different parts of the page. When you get to something that you want to use, like a link or button, press <bold>Enter</bold>.
Resources/SecondWelcomePage_Paragraph1_T: Welcome back. If you ever want to revisit this guide, select "Open Narrator Home" in your Narrator settings, then select "QuickStart." You'll also find a link to the complete Narrator guide there.
Resources/SecondWelcomePage_Paragraph2_T: To go through this guide again, press <bold>Enter</bold> on the <bold>Resume guide</bold> button.
Resources/SecondWelcomePage_Paragraph3_T: Remember, to turn Narrator on or off, press and hold the <bold>Windows logo</bold> key, then press <bold>Ctrl</bold> and <bold>Enter</bold>. To stop reading, press <bold>Ctrl</bold>. Then, use the <bold>Up</bold> or <bold>Down arrow</bold> keys to keep reading from where Narrator left off.

Resources/SummaryPage_Paragraph1_Text: Congratulations. You've reached the end of this guide. We hope it was helpful. Each section is linked below, so you can review it again if you want.
Resources/SummaryPage_Paragraph2_Text: When you're ready to dive deeper, you can check out the <hyperlink id='UserGuideLink' url='https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/p/?linkid=873381'>Narrator user guide</hyperlink> for even more info.​
Resources/TextBlock10_Text: Press <bold>Caps + F1</bold> to hear a full list of Narrator commands. To learn more, press the <bold>Windows logo key + Ctrl + N</bold> to open your Narrator settings and access the online user guide.
Resources/TextBlock2_Text: Your keyboard is a tool that can help you control Narrator. Narrator commands are often abbreviated like this: <bold>Narrator key + 1</bold>. This means press and hold <bold>the Narrator key</bold>, then press the number <bold>1</bold> key. This command turns on input learning, which tells you what keys you're pressing, as well as the Narrator command associated with them. To turn it off, press <bold>Narrator key + 1</bold> twice. You can use Caps lock or Insert as your Narrator key.
Resources/TextBlock4_Text: Even when you're not using a screen reader like Narrator, you can use your keyboard to get around pages and apps.
Resources/TextBlock5_Text: To move between controls on a page, like check boxes and buttons, press <bold>Tab</bold> or <bold>Shift + Tab</bold>.
Resources/TextBlock6_Text: To switch between apps, press <bold>Alt + Tab</bold>. You may need to hold down <bold>Alt</bold> and press the <bold>Tab</bold> key several times to find the app you want.
Resources/TextBlock7_Text: To search for an app, press the <bold>Windows logo key</bold>, type the name of the app, and choose it from the list. Use the <bold>Up</bold> and <bold>Down</bold> arrow keys to explore lists.
Resources/TextBlock8_Text: To close an app, press <bold>Alt + F4</bold>.

You'll notice that the <bold>Up</bold> and <bold>Down arrow</bold> keys, commands, and heading and landmark navigation will keep you within the webpage's content area. Once you leave the webpage, Narrator will go back to reading everything that's on your screen.

Once you enter the webpage, all Narrator reading and navigation commands will move you around the webpage's content. This lets you focus on what's inside the webpage, instead of all the info on the screen.

Resources/TryWebpagePage_Paragraph4_Text: To review individual text characters, press the <bold>Left</bold> and <bold>Right arrow</bold> keys.
Resources/TryWebpagePage_Paragraph5_Text: To read word by word, press <bold>Ctrl + Left arrow</bold> or <bold>Ctrl + Right arrow</bold>.
Resources/TryWebpagePage_Paragraph6_Text: To move between headings, press the <bold>H key</bold>, or <bold>Shift + H</bold>.
Resources/TryWebpagePage_Paragraph7_Text: To move between landmarks, press the <bold>D key</bold>, or <bold>Shift + D</bold>.
Resources/TryWebpagePage_Paragraph8_Text: To move to the address bar, press <bold>Alt + D</bold> or <bold>Ctrl + L</bold>.
Resources/TryWebpagePage_Paragraph9_Text: Once you hear Narrator say, "search or enter web address, editing," enter the word "more" to bring up a list of suggestions. Press the <bold>Up</bold> and <bold>Down arrow</bold> keys to move through the options, and press <bold>Enter</bold> to choose one. All the options will take you to the same webpage.

Fast and healthyClassic Margherita Pizza with Basil and Fresh MozzarellaTime to Prepare25 min.

A thin crust is the hallmark of this archetypal pizza dish. If it's too thick, you might lose the nuance of the simple flavors that make this a classic. The key is balance: Avoid overloading any one topping or flavor. Instead, let the simple ingredients blend harmoniously.\n

Ingredients

Select all ingredients

Pizza Dough Napolitana

  • Stir warm water (just above room temperature), yeast and sugar together in a large bowl, then let stand until the yeast is dissolved (3–5 minutes).
  • Stir in bread flour (or other high-elastic flour), whole grain flour and salt until the dough begins to form. This dough will be slightly more wet than normal bread dough. Let the dough sit for about 5 min.
  • Turn the dough out onto a floured counter top or other work surface. Knead the dough until it feels smooth and elastic (usually around 10 minutes).
  • Add approximately 2 tablespoons of olive oil to a large bowl. Place the dough in the bowl and turn until the surface of the dough has been completely coated. Add approximately 2 tablespoons of olive oil to a large bowl. Place the dough in the bowl and turn until the surface of the dough has been completely coated.
  • Cover the bowl with plastic wrap or a clean towel and set it aside to rise. The ideal location is warm, dry and draft-free. The dough is ready once it has doubled in size, approximately one hour.

    • Minimalist Margherita

  • Classic Neapolitan pizza cooks off the radiant heat of a pizza stone. Place your stone on a rack in the bottom third of the oven and preheat 500°F. Allow the stone to absorb heat in the oven for at least 20 minutes once you've reached that temperature.
  • Divide the dough in half and place on a floured surface. Roll each into a 12-inch circle.
  • Place toppings on the rolled-out crust. Classic toppings include Roma tomatoes and mozzarella slices. If you want to add sauce, try our Better than Mom's Pizza Sauce recipe, made from fresh tomatoes and basil—but know that you'll be bucking tradition!
  • Drizzle olive oil the tomatoes and top with torn basil. The basil is most flavorful if you tear it just before placing the pizza in the oven.
  • Use a floured pizza peel to transfer the dough to your pizza stone. Leave the pizza stone in the oven and be careful. It's going to be hot!
  • Let the dough bake. The crust should rise within 2 minutes and brown within 5 minutes. Watch it carefully and get a feel for the right moment to take it out of the oven.
  • Remove the crust from the oven. Combine another tablespoon of olive oil with the garlic and brush the outer ring of the crust as a final garnish and flavor. Cool for about five minutes before serving.
